text:
IncidentBot: 🚨 Elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate (gateway 502/504s) — error rate 11.8% over 5m, paging on-call SRE

Alice Chen: oncall here, seeing alerts. Confirming scope: most errors are gateway 504 + backend 5xx (502/503). Any major deploys in last 30m?

Marco Rivera: no deploys from runtime in last hour. I see a giant spike in prefix_kv miss rate and eviction churn around 09:14 UTC. Putting quick graphs: prefix_cache.miss_rate -> from 0.4% -> 28% at spike.

Priya Patel: sending logs snippet. Looks like many prefix lookups returning inconsistent values (empty blobs) causing downstream deserial errors: `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError` in model-router. Also seeing long tail latencies on redis-kv-proxy.

Marco Rivera: paste logs:
```
09:13:47 model-router: prefix_lookup id=abc123 status=OK size=0
09:13:47 model-router: prefix_lookup id=abc124 status=OK size=0
09:13:47 model-router: decode_error id=abc125 error=JSONDecodeError
09:13:48 kv-proxy: eviction event keys=12k rate=500/s
09:13:49 front-gateway: upstream 502 from model-router
```

Samir Gupta: sounds like a prefix cache corruption/eviction storm causing a thundering herd of read-throughs. That spikes latency and triggers gateway timeouts. Could be a bad compaction on shard X or memory pressure on nodes.

Alice Chen: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip `prefix_cache.read_through=true` -> false (force read-through disabled, i.e., serve from slow store only) 2) invalidate suspect prefix ranges 3) fail open to fallback small-model variant 4) autoscale runtime pool. Which is safest to apply quickly?

Priya Patel: I vote invalidate ranges + temporarily disable read-through. Disabling read-through prevents repeated heavy reads to backing store while we clean up. I'll prepare the flag toggle.

Dan O'Neill: I'll run invalidate command for suspect prefixes. Running admin API: `POST /admin/cache/invalidate` with prefix regex. Example I'm about to run:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://admin.redwood.internal/admin/cache/invalidate \
  -d '{"prefix_regex":"^userprefix:2026-03-14:.*"}'
```

deploy-bot: Start rollout: feature-flag toggle `runtime.prefix_cache.read_through=false` by Dan O'Neill — 1/3 nodes updated.

Dan O'Neill: completed invalidate for prefixes matching the regex on shard-a and shard-b. Leaving shard-c for safe window to avoid mass-miss.

Marco Rivera: after invalidate + read_through=false, I'm seeing miss_rate drop quickly and 5xx%. Early numbers: error rate down from 11.8% -> 3.1% in 4m. Gateway 504s reduced.

Alice Chen: good. Customers still seeing intermittent errors; CS, can you surface which accounts?

Customer Success: CustomerOps: A few customers reported increased latency and 502s: acct-172 (high QPS), acct-301 (batching). We've opened tickets for both. We'll send a proactive PSAT to acct-172.

Priya Patel: root cause theory so far — KV prefix index got corrupted during a background compaction on shard-b when memory pressure caused premature evictions. That produced empty blobs for some prefixes; model-router treats empty as ok then fails on parse later. Patch candidate: add validation on read and fallback to origin if payload invalid. Also add a soft lock during compaction to avoid serving stale pointers.

Samir Gupta: longer-term: add metrics alert for prefix_blob_size==0 + correlate with eviction events. Also consider incremental invalidate + backoff to avoid eviction storms causing thundering-herd.

Alice Chen: ops checklist for handoff — 1) Priya will keep monitoring runtime for 30m 2) Marco to run KV integrity check on shard-b and snapshot suspect keys 3) Dan to create rollback/patch PR for safe compaction 4) CS to update customers with mitigation details 5) open postmortem in incidents channel.

Marco Rivera: kicking off `kv-inspect --shard shard-b --check-empty-blobs --output /tmp/inspect-177912.log` now. ETA ~12m. I'll attach findings.

Support Ops: adding a customer-facing blurb for status page noting partial degradation and mitigations. ETA 10m.

IncidentBot: Metrics check — error rate stabilized at ~2.9% over last 5m after toggles. Continue monitoring.

Alice Chen: handing off to Priya (next oncall) for watch. Priya, take ownership for postmortem + confirm when KV checks complete. I'll update incident and mark this as "mitigated" once shard integrity confirmed.

Priya Patel: taking handoff. Will supervise the integrity run and follow up on PR for compaction safety. I'll update here in 30.

Dan O'Neill: created PR #4231 for compaction lock + validation, link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4231 — includes unit tests for empty-blob detection.

Marco Rivera: `kv-inspect` results: found ~4.2k keys with zero-length payloads on shard-b (not present on a/b backups). Extracted suspect keylist to s3://redwood-debug/inspect-177912-keys.csv.

Priya Patel: plan: run targeted rehydrate for those keys from backup store (read from object-store origin) and then re-enable read_through gradually. Schedule window for rehydrate in 20m; will throttle to avoid another storm.

Customer Success: sending update to acct-172 and acct-301 that we mitigated service errors, transient issues remain while we rehydrate prefixes. We'll offer dedicated support until keys restored.

Alice Chen: marking as mitigated for now. We have live mitigation in place (flag toggles + invalidation) and a remediation path (rehydrate + compaction fix). Priya — please run final verification and file postmortem with timeline + impact numbers.

Priya Patel: will do. Closing live incident thread, moving to postmortem thread now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
